fatal_errors: The proposed TiN/CrN coating is unrelated to the target intervention of varying Mo content in a Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3-containing CoCrFeNiMox composite.
The cited evidence does not demonstrate that TiN or CrN coatings on CoCrFeNi remain adherent, lubricious, and wear-resistant from room temperature through 800 °C.
The intervention is not uniquely specified: coating chemistry, thickness, deposition method, adhesion, and oxidation stability are all left undefined.
The claimed 30% friction and 50% wear reductions are unsupported by the cited evidence.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad wide-temperature tribology problem and includes a comparative falsification test, but it does not reconstruct the studied material or intervention. The target uses Mo variation to induce FCC lattice distortion and a hard sigma phase within a composite containing Ni/MoS2, Ag, and Cr2O3; lubrication changes from MoS2/Ag-rich films at low-to-medium temperature to compact NiO/silver-molybdate glaze films at high temperature. The generated mechanism invokes only a generic protective oxide and therefore does not explain low-temperature lubrication, intermediate-temperature degradation, or the role of Mo strengthening and molybdate formation. Conditions agree only in temperature span: the proposed 5 N reciprocating test at 1 Hz differs from the 8 N, 0.15 m/s, 270 m ball-on-disk test in air against Si3N4. Its uncoated CoCrFeNi baseline also omits the actual Mo0.2 composite baseline and provides no quantitative baseline data. E1 and E2 support adaptive glaze formation in a different alloy architecture, while E3 concerns load-dependent oxidation of CoCrFeMnNi; none directly validates TiN/CrN coating performance. The paired coated/uncoated experiment could detect a performance difference, but arbitrary thresholds and absent coating characterization, environmental controls, counterface specification, replication, and post-wear phase analysis limit its discriminability.
